gap: The learning rate and momentum for full-batch SGD on Breast Cancer logistic regression are not specified.
chosen: constant learning rate 0.1 with no momentum
rationale: 0.1 lies inside the paper's reported 0.05–0.5 sweep range and is a conventional full-batch LR for standardized logistic regression.
quote: Learning-rate sweeps (0.05–0.5) do not rescue the uncompensated variants.

gap: The number of training epochs and the stopping criterion are not stated.
chosen: 200 full-batch epochs with early stop when relative train-loss change <1e-6
rationale: The paper reports convergence parity but does not publish an epoch count; 200 epochs is enough for small CPU-scale logistic regression and the tolerance avoids overfitting.

gap: The logistic-regression penalty/regularization is not specified.
rationale: The paper names logistic regression among standard losses without stating a penalty; unregularized cross-entropy is the minimal faithful choice for reproducing the baseline.
quote: logistic regression, linear SVM, softmax regression, and a one-hidden-layer MLP

gap: Whether feature standardization is fit on the training split only or on the full dataset is not stated.
options: fit scaler on training split only
chosen: fit StandardScaler on the training split only and transform the test split
rationale: Avoids train/test leakage and follows standard practice for a 75/25 split.
quote: N = 0.3, α = 0.3 unless stated; 75/25 stratified splits; standardized features

gap: It is ambiguous whether epoch-t masks use epoch-(t−1) stored losses or current-epoch losses, since the protocol says current losses but the library uses delayed losses.
options: use stored previous-epoch losses for epoch-t masks
use current-epoch losses after a full forward pass
use a fixed threshold from initial losses
chosen: use stored epoch-(t−1) losses to form epoch-t masks and recompute the 40th percentile on those stored losses
rationale: This matches the released library's delayed-losses description and preserves the claimed forward-pass saving for excluded samples.
quote: delayed-losses pattern (masks for epoch t built from epoch t−1 losses; released with the library) removes even the forward of excluded samples

gap: The exact weighted without-replacement sampling algorithm and finite-sample inclusion probabilities are not fully algorithmic.
options: np.random.choice with p=pi and replace=False; use πi=m pi
systematic PPS sampling; use πi=m pi
rejective sampling with exact inclusion probabilities
chosen: np.random.choice with defensive-mixture probabilities without replacement for m draws; use πi=m pi in the Hajek weights
rationale: The paper explicitly invokes the Poisson/rejective approximation and specifies single-draw probabilities but not a unique sampler; this is the direct implementation.
quote: Draw S ⊂M, |S| = m, without replacement with single-draw probabilities

gap: Table 1 prints a single value and a spread, but the aggregation rule for a single reproduction is not explicit beyond paired seeds.
chosen: report mean test accuracy over seeds 0–4
rationale: The paper says seeds 0–4 are paired throughout, so the reported number is the paired multi-seed mean.
quote: Seeds are published and paired across methods (seeds 0–4 throughout; 0–9 for Table 3)

gap: The per-sample loss used for logistic regression is not formally specified.
chosen: binary cross-entropy on the sigmoid output
rationale: The paper groups logistic, softmax, and squared losses and uses loss thresholds; binary cross-entropy is the standard logistic-regression loss.
quote: for the standard losses used here (logistic, softmax, squared), the per-sample gradient factorizes as

gap: The population over which the 40th-percentile threshold is computed is not fully pinned down.
chosen: all training-set per-sample losses from the previous epoch
rationale: The protocol says per-epoch recalibration at the 40th percentile of current losses; with delayed masks the current available full set is the previous epoch's stored losses.
quote: per-epoch recalibration of K at the 40th percentile of current losses

gap: For α=0.3, exact inclusion probabilities under without-replacement sampling are not computed.
rationale: Assumption 1(b) explicitly authorizes this approximation for α<1, and the paper measures its residual bias as small.
quote: we use the Poisson/rejective approximation πi = m pi, standard for high-entropy without-replacement designs

gap: The synthetic fraud replica's class covariance, exact positive count, and split details are not fully specified.
options: isotropic unit-variance Gaussians with exact 34 positives
shared empirical covariance from a real fraud set
chosen: isotropic unit-variance Gaussians, exact 34 positives (0.17% of 20,000), 75/25 stratified split
rationale: The paper gives means, n, d, and imbalance but not covariance; isotropic Gaussians with the stated mean shift are the minimal generator.
quote: 0.17% positives, n = 20,000, d = 15, Gaussian classes with mean shift 1.2

gap: How 40% symmetric label noise is applied is not detailed.
options: flip 40% of training labels uniformly to the other class
flip 40% of all labels including test
flip each training label independently with probability 0.4
chosen: flip exactly 40% of training labels uniformly to the other class, fixed per seed
rationale: Symmetric flips on training labels are the usual interpretation and keep the test set clean for evaluation.
quote: at 40% symmetric flips on Breast Cancer, accuracy collapses to 0.386 (baseline 0.832; v3 0.808)

gap: The initialization of logistic-regression weights is not stated.
rationale: Standard for convex logistic regression and deterministic across paired seeds; paired data ordering and split still control comparison.

gap: Whether all samples are forward-passed each epoch or only retained samples are forward-passed is not explicit in the protocol.
options: forward all samples to compute losses and mask
forward only retained samples using delayed masks
chosen: forward all samples for loss scoring in the baseline reproduction, while excluding backward passes only for non-retained minors
rationale: The central compute saving is defined as backward-pass saving; using delayed masks changes forward cost but not the reported backward fraction.
quote: The number of backward passes per iteration is (n −k) + m
